The Manager

Mumbai 400 051 
The General Manager 
Dept. of Corporate Services

P. J. Towers, Dalal Street 
Mumbai 400 001 
 
Dear Sirs, 
 
Scheme of Amalgamation of Sproutlife Foods Private Limited with the Company  
 
We write to advise that the Board of Directors of the Company at the meeting held today  
i.e., 2nd November, 2026 has approved the Scheme of Amalgamation of Sproutlife Foods 
Private Limited, a wholly owned subsidiary, with the Company under Sections 230 and 232 of 
the Companies Act, 2013. 
 
The aforesaid Scheme of Amalgamation, which is subject to necessary approvals, will take 
effect from 1st April, 2026. 
 
Enclosed please find the relevant disclosure pursuant to Regulation 30 of the  
SEBI (Listing Obligations and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 2015 read with the  
SEBI Master Circular dated 30th January, 2026. 
 
The Board Meeting commenced at 2.45 p.m. and concluded at 6.05 p.m. 
 
Yours faithfully,  
ITC Limited 
 
 
 
(R. K. Singhi) 
Executive Vice President & 
Company Secretary 
 
Encl. as above. 
 
RAJENDRA

Sproutlife, being a wholly owned subsidiary, is a related party of 
ITC.  
Transfer of all assets, liabilities, rights, obligations and employees 
of Sproutlife to ITC, as part of the proposal for amalgamation, will 
be at arm’s length. 
3.  Area of business of the 
entities 
Transferor Company: 
Sproutlife is primarily engaged in the business of manufacture and 
sale of food products, including bars, muesli, oats, protein-rich 
foods and peanut butter, catering to health-conscious consumers 
under the new-age, digital-first brand ‘Yoga Bar’. 
 
Transferee Company: 
ITC is one of India’s leading private sector companies and a 
diversified conglomerate with businesses spanning Fast Moving 
Consumer Goods (Cigarettes & Cigars, Branded Packaged Foods, 
Personal Care Products, Education & Stationery Products, Safety 
Matches and Agarbattis), Paperboards, Paper and Packaging, and 
Agri Business. 
4.  Rationale 
for 
amalgamation / merger 
The proposed amalgamation of Sproutlife with ITC will,  
inter alia, have the following benefits: 
(a) Enable seamless integration of business operations of both the 
companies, thereby unlocking the full potential of the combined 
business 
operations 
and 
maximising 
value 
creation 
opportunities through realisation of synergies; 
(b) Achieve optimal deployment of financial, managerial and 
operational resources across the combined business operations 
by accessing the shared talent pool and common resources; 
(c) Enhance efficiency of capital allocation by consolidating and 
optimising the cash flows and financial resources of both the 
companies; and 
(d) Result in reduction of the number of operating entities to 
simplify the corporate holding structure.
